item.text: I’m reading the current four-file layout first to find the next structural change that still improves the design instead of just moving names around. After that I’ll edit and rerun the program.

I found a decent next refactor target: edge endpoints are still passed around as raw `int, int` pairs everywhere, which keeps graph construction and conversion low-level. I’m introducing a small edge value type and routing graph creation through it so construction becomes more declarative.
The edge value type is in place. I’m compiling the expanded file set and running the program now to confirm the new construction path is still behavior-preserving.

I refactored graph construction around an explicit edge value type by adding [DirectedEdge.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/029_detect_cycle_directed_graph/DirectedEdge.java).

`DirectedGraph` now has `fromEdges(int, List<DirectedEdge>)`, `DirectedGraphBuilder` can add a `DirectedEdge` directly, and [DetectCycleDirectedGraph.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/029_detect_cycle_directed_graph/DetectCycleDirectedGraph.java) defines its sample graph as a declarative edge list instead of a chain of raw integer calls. That removes some low-level construction noise and gives the codebase a clearer representation for “an edge” as data.

Verification: `javac DetectCycleDirectedGraph.java DirectedGraph.java DirectedGraphBuilder.java DirectedEdge.java CycleDetector.java` succeeded, and `java DetectCycleDirectedGraph` still prints `true`.
